rationale: Bounding the effect just measured, from source rather than by leaving it open. The live-cluster receipt shows an unconfigured sender costing a healthy three-voter cluster its serving leader, and the discriminator now asks whether that loss is permanent. The captured election path answers part of it: only the restarted node adopted the higher term, while the other voters of the configuration in force keep the lower term and their known leader until their own election timers fire, at which point a voter of the configuration can campaign and win with a quorum of that configuration; the empty-configuration node itself contributes nothing but a vote it grants to any candidate, which is already measured. That makes the measured outsider effect a leadership interruption whose duration is set by the surviving voters' election timers rather than an unrecoverable loss, and this statement is source-derived from the cited follower and candidate ranges, not measured. Nothing else in the account, the knowledge entries or the citations is changed.

interpretations.joint_history: Five receipts now answer this question from one recovery state, an empty configuration after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart. Two runs state the vote and pre-vote admission (f418b9d6ab8841faa9ab6c35ce1fcd75 and e1ee764584564a95b3e288381dfb75d9 at indices 6 and 7), one states the leadership acceptance and the election-gating control in a single-node cluster (e87ee87274544b3ba836dffb93a7ecb1 at indices 19 and 20), one states the entry path (7e6d5b3d49464a84ba43f7f9305ea5b6 at indices 19, 20 and 21), and the newest run (e52401f293244c72ae4e1dcb5f6889dd at indices 37 and 38) states the same behaviour inside a live three-voter cluster, where only the outsider contact is now measured rather than argued.
interpretations.rationale: Current account: an empty recovered configuration removes participation checks on every path the question covers, while the node's own participation is gated off, and in a live cluster the node both converges on the legitimate leader and remains usable to an outsider. Measured in the newest receipt (e52401f293244c72ae4e1dcb5f6889dd at events 37 and 38): after the restart the node held an empty configuration with no leader; the serving leader's heartbeats restored its leader view and it stored a command committed after the restart (log index 10 to 11) while its configuration stayed empty and it stayed a follower; then one AppendEntries request with no entries from a server that appears in no configuration, carrying the node's term plus five, was accepted, the outsider became the node's leader, the node's term rose to 7 and the serving leader of the healthy three-voter cluster stepped down with no leader present at that moment. Mechanism from source: appendEntries applies no membership test to the sender and records it as leader while adopting its term, and the follower loop only clears a known leader when contact stops, so heartbeat contact from the legitimate leader converges the node's leader view but does not repair the configuration; an arriving configuration entry is the repair path measured elsewhere. Vote and pre-vote admission and the entry path stay as recorded in the earlier receipts. Bound on the measured outsider effect, newly derived from the same cited ranges: only the restarted node adopted the higher term, so the voters of the configuration in force keep their term and their known leader until their own election timers fire, after which a voter can campaign and win a quorum of that configuration; the restarted node can give an outsider a vote, which is already measured, but it cannot itself campaign with an empty configuration. The effect measured in receipt e52401f293244c72ae4e1dcb5f6889dd is therefore a leadership interruption whose length follows from the surviving voters' election timers rather than a permanent loss of leadership, and this bound is source-derived rather than measured, since the receipt ends at the moment the serving leader stepped down with no leader present.
counterevidence: The empty-list leniency in the vote handlers is intentional for cluster bootstrap, and appendEntries has always trusted the sender's identity; what makes both harmful here is that the node's own recovery produces an empty configuration in a cluster that is not being bootstrapped.

The measured outsider effect is a leadership change, not a log or data change: the outsider sent no entries and the node's log content was unchanged by that request, and the request itself is a legal protocol message rather than a forged one.
The node's own election gating is intact, so the failure is asymmetric: it admits others while suppressing itself, which also means it cannot repair the configuration by winning an election.

Convergence bound measured in the same receipt: because the legitimate leader kept heartbeating, the node's recorded leader was restored to that leader, so the outsider effect needs a sender that reaches the node while the legitimate leader is quiet, which is the ordering the probe created.
limitations: Measured with the repository's in-memory transport and stores; production transports, authentication and network behaviour are not covered, and the outsider needed only transport reachability.
The entry phase used one command entry with no configuration semantics, so the FSM effect recorded is a single applied command.
The probe does not measure how long the empty configuration persists in a cluster without membership traffic; that follows from the repair path rather than from a timed observation.

The live-cluster run uses one three-voter in-memory cluster with timers shortened to 200 ms, one restarted follower and one outsider request; whether the cluster recovered a leader after the displacement was not measured, and the term the outsider could impose through a single quiet window is not bounded in time.

The bound on the outsider effect is source-derived from the captured election path: the receipt stops at the step-down, so neither the interval without a leader nor the term at which the cluster re-elects is measured.
